name: Workplace Safety Checklist
description: A general workplace safety program covering hazards, PPE, training, emergencies and records.

items.text: Walk each work area and document physical, chemical and ergonomic hazards.
Confirm a job hazard analysis exists for higher-risk tasks.
Verify controls follow the hierarchy: eliminate, substitute, engineer, then PPE.
items.note: Treat PPE as the last line of defense, not the first.

items.text: Check that reported hazards are logged and tracked to closure.
Confirm machine guards, interlocks and barriers are in place and working.
Review near-miss reports for trends and recurring risks.
Confirm a PPE hazard assessment has been completed and documented.
Check the correct PPE is available, sized and worn for each task.
Verify PPE is inspected, maintained and replaced when damaged.
Confirm tools and equipment are inspected and removed from service when faulty.
items.note: Tag and isolate defective equipment so it cannot be used by mistake.

items.text: Check that safety devices and guards have not been bypassed.
Confirm new hires receive safety orientation before starting work.
Verify task-specific and refresher training is current and recorded.
Check that safety data sheets are accessible to all employees.
Confirm toolbox talks or safety meetings are held and documented.
Verify employees know how to report hazards and incidents.
Check warning, mandatory and prohibition signs are posted and legible.
Confirm exits, hazards and equipment are clearly labeled.
Verify walkways and work areas are clear of clutter and trip hazards.
Check spills are cleaned promptly and absorbents are available.
items.note: Keep aisles, exits and electrical panels unobstructed at all times.

items.text: Confirm waste and chemicals are stored and disposed of correctly.
Confirm the emergency action plan is documented and current.
Check fire extinguishers, alarms and emergency lighting are working.
Verify first aid kits are stocked and first aiders are trained.
Confirm evacuation routes, exits and assembly points are clear and posted.
Check that a recent drill has been carried out and logged.
Review provisions for visitors, contractors and anyone needing evacuation assistance.
Confirm injury and illness records are maintained as required.
Check that inspections and corrective actions are documented and dated.
Verify training records are complete and up to date.
Confirm equipment inspection and maintenance logs are kept.
Review the program annually and after any incident or process change.
Important: this is general guidance only and does not replace OSHA regulations, formal training or your employer's safety program; confirm requirements with a qualified person.

faq.q: How often should the workplace safety program be reviewed?
faq.a: Review the full program at least annually, and sooner after an incident, a new process, or a change in equipment or staffing. Inspect high-risk areas and emergency equipment more frequently.

faq.q: Who is responsible for workplace safety?
faq.a: Employers hold overall responsibility, usually delegated to a safety officer or manager. Every employee must follow safe procedures and report hazards, but one person should own the program and its follow-up.

faq.q: What are the core elements of a safety program?
faq.a: Hazard identification and control, written procedures, PPE, training, clear signage, emergency preparedness, incident reporting and recordkeeping are the building blocks most safety programs share.

faq.q: Can this checklist be adapted to my industry?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF and tailor it to your operation, adding hazard-specific items such as machine guarding, lockout/tagout, confined spaces or hazardous chemicals as your workplace requires.

faq.q: Does this replace OSHA standards or professional advice?
faq.a: No. It is general guidance and does not replace OSHA regulations, formal safety training, your employer's safety program, or a qualified person. Always confirm the standards that apply to your workplace.
